title: Introduce delegation-path verifier, KMS consent fanout and compact audit envelope
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds an opt-in delegation-path verifier and KMS consent fanout with compact audit envelope support. Backwards compatible guardrails and a staged rollout are included.
description: Motivation: Several customers and compliance reviews highlighted a gap where operator-delegation chains could be used to escalate cross-tenant signing without clear provenance. This PR adds a lightweight delegation-path verifier that enforces chain constraints at the policy layer, a KMS consent fanout to coordinate multi-region key consent for operations touching residency-sensitive resources, and a compact audit envelope to reduce payload size while preserving non-repudiable proofs. Goals: 1) Prevent unintended cross-tenant operator delegation by verifying the explicit path and required endorsements before KMS operations; 2) Allow KMS requests that span multiple configured consent anchors to fanout consent checks and aggregate results; 3) Produce a compact, signed audit envelope for high-throughput audit ingestion to improve retention and storage costs. Summary of changes: - policy/delegation_verifier: new module that validates delegation chains, applies allow/deny heuristics, and emits decision rationale into the trace header. - k8s/operator-adapter: wire up a pre-commit hook to call the verifier for operator-scoped requests. - kms/consent_fanout: new service that fans out consent checks to configured KMS consent providers (primary region + fallbacks) and returns a consolidated decision with per-provider attestations. - audit/envelope_v2: introduce a compact envelope schema (base64-encoded canonical header + signatures) and a serializer compatible with the existing ingest pipeline. - console: small UX additions to show delegation path failures and per-request consent breakdowns in the request inspector. - e2e and unit tests: coverage for path validation permutations, consent fanout happy/failure paths, and envelope roundtrip. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear (ENG-4872) - [x] Unit tests for verifier and fanout - [x] e2e tests in perf-canary that simulate geo failover - [x] Backwards compatibility: envelope_v2 defaults to optional; older consumers continue to read envelope_v1 - [x] Observability: added metrics for verifier rejections, fanout latency distribution, envelope compression ratio - [ ] Docs: console help text and developer guide update (follow-up PR) Commits summary: - Add delegation verifier core logic and tests - Introduce KMS consent fanout service and mock adapters - Implement compact audit envelope V2 + serializer/decoder - Hook verifier into operator-adapter and add metric instrumentation - Add canary deployment configuration and rollout script Changed areas (high-level): - policy/delegation_verifier/{verifier.go,verifier_test.go,README.md} - kms/consent_fanout/{service.go,adapters/mock_adapter.go,adapters/aws_adapter.go} - audit/envelope_v2/{schema.go,serializer.go,ingest_compat_test.go} - operators/operator-adapter/{precommit_hook.go,metrics.go} - console/src/components/RequestInspector/DelegationPanel.tsx - infra/helm/redwood-canary-delegation.yaml Migration and rollout: This is an opt-in feature behind two feature flags: rbac.delegation_verifier.enabled and kms.consent_fanout.enabled. The audit envelope v2 is opt-in via client-specified Accept header (Accept: application/vnd.redwood.audit.v2+json) and an ingest-side switch for envelope indexing. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy services to canary region with flags off by default. 2) Enable delegation_verifier in shadow mode (log decisions, do not deny) for 72 hours and monitor verifier.rejection_rate and false_positive alerts. 3) Enable hard deny for configured tenants incrementally (10% of operator traffic -> 50% -> 100%) with rollback thresholds on rejection_rate and 5xx ratio. 4) Enable kms.consent_fanout for a small set of high-sensitivity routes and monitor fanout.latency_p50/p95 and consent_provider_failure_count. 5) Start advertising envelope_v2 to internal consumers and run compatibility ingestion for a week before enabling at scale. Monitoring & alerts: - New metrics: verifier.rejections_total{reason}, verifier.latency_ms, fanout.requests_total, fanout.latency_ms_bucket, envelope_v2.compression_ratio - Alerts: verifier.surge (30m > 0.5% rejection rate), fanout.failed_providers (>3 providers fail in 5m), envelope.decompress_error_rate (>0.1% on ingest) Backwards compatibility and safety nets: - Verifier runs in shadow mode for observation before hard enforcement. - Consent fanout supports conservative fail-closed or fail-open modes configured per-tenant; default is fail-closed for residency protected tenants. - Envelope v2 can be toggled per-tenant and has a compatibility shim on ingest that expands compact envelopes for downstream tools. Testing: Unit tests (added) cover typical delegation graphs, cycle detection, TTL enforcement on delegation edges, and signature verification for propagated endorsements. Integration tests include a mocked multi-KMS environment (AWS-like + in-house consent service) to simulate partial failures and verify fanout consolidation behavior. Performance: Benchmarks show verifier adds median 1.2ms CPU overhead per operator request (shadow mode) and fanout adds an extra 12ms p50 when using two consent adapters in parallel; we added caching of consent decisions for 30s for identical request fingerprints to reduce tail latency. Security review notes: Implemented strict canonicalization for envelope signing; included non-replay nonce and per-tenant key id in the signature context. We used HMAC-SHA256 signing for internal envelope attestations and delegated to KMS for any customer CMK signatures. Review highlights and resolution: - Request from Ravi to add cycle detection and explicit TTL on delegation edges -> implemented and tested. - Leah requested clearer metrics labels and a separate tag for tenant-protected requests -> updated instrumentation. - Omar asked for explicit fail-open configuration per-tenant for non-residency tenants -> added config and unit tests. Known limitations: - Consent fanout currently implements two adapters (aws-like and mock); adding GCP/Azure adapters is tracked in ENG-5231. - Envelope_v2 does not yet support streaming ingestion; tracked in ENG-5290. Follow-ups: docs PR for developer guide and console help (SEC-122), add GCP consent adapter (ENG-5231), streaming ingest support for envelope_v2 (ENG-5290).
